53, 9–16, 2017 Design of Carbon Nanotube-Based Broadband Radar Absorber for Ka-Band Frequency Range 1, 2, * 1 1 1, 3 Dzmitry Bychanok , Gleb Gorokhov , Darya Meisak , Polina Kuzhir , 1, 2 4 4 4 4 Sergey Maksimenko , Yongliang Wang , Zhidong Han , Xin Gao , and Hongyan Yue Abstract—The general principles of design and development of microwave absorbing materials are discussed and analysed in respect to 26–37GHz frequency range (Ka-band)
Both theoretical and experimental results demonstrate that presented composites may be used as compact effective absorbers in 26–37GHz range

For development of 5G communication systems, it is necessary to solve many problems related to electromagnetic compatibility and develop materials effectively absorbing electromagnetic radiation at high frequencies
Many researchers worldwide concentrate on the design of absorbers for various frequency ranges [1–9]

A great number of investigations show that nanocarbon materials have excellent electromagnetic properties to be used for production of composite materials with controlled electromagnetic properties [10–14]
In the present paper, we use carbon nanotube-based composites to produce an effective broadband absorber for Ka-band region (26–37GHz)
In contrast to our recent work [7], here we consider electromagnetic properties of composites with concentration of inclusions above percolation threshold

So the materials under study are macroscopically conductive with a static conductivity of “several Siemens per meter” and have pronounced frequency dispersion of dielectric permittivity ε ∼1/ν, which is optimal for design of microwave absorbers [1]
The first-principle equations describing the electromagnetic response of such a system in free space are well known [15,16]
